claims.text: The baseline intermediate-layer material is a CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy.
The baseline CoCrFeNiMn alloy has a uniform microstructure and no secondary high-conductivity phase.
Adding a minor amount of Ag and heat treating at approximately 750–800°C for 10–30 minutes under inert atmosphere with controlled cooling will induce a low-volume fraction of Ag nanoprecipitates.
The proposed thermal treatment will favor coherent or semi-coherent Ag precipitate formation in the CoCrFeNiMn matrix.
The Ag nanoprecipitates will preferentially decorate grain boundaries and intragranular regions.
The Ag nanoprecipitates will form a continuous nanoscale network.
Silver has very high electronic thermal conductivity.
A finely dispersed coherent Ag network in the HEA matrix will provide additional heat-transfer paths.
Well-bonded Ag–matrix interfaces will maintain mechanical load transfer and minimize crack initiation.
The Ag-modified alloy will preserve overall structural integrity under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
The Ag-modified alloy will exhibit an approximately 30–50% increase in effective thermal conductivity relative to the unmodified alloy.
The Ag-modified alloy will maintain thermal-fatigue resistance comparable to that of the unmodified alloy.
The Ag-modified alloy will maintain resistance to structural degradation comparable to that of the unmodified alloy.
The unmodified CoCrFeNiMn intermediate layer has lower heat-transfer efficiency because it lacks a dedicated high-conductivity phase.
The proposed performance improvement should hold at steady-state temperatures up to 600°C under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The proposed performance improvement may hold under moderate irradiation.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is 30–50%, but the falsification rule parenthetically says it is 'targeting <30% improvement.' The intended threshold appears to be that an improvement below 30% falsifies the hypothesis, so the written inequality is inconsistent or ambiguous.
